info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package flags is feature flags: ship it dark, then turn it on for who you pick.

post.summary: Runs the caller's flag definitions for one identity and returns the flag verdict: which flags are on (or which variant), their payloads, and whether any definition failed to compute.
post.description:
Runs the caller's flag definitions for one identity and returns the
flag verdict: which flags are on (or which variant), their payloads,
and whether any definition failed to compute. Evaluation is in-process over the
caller's own (org, project) definitions — no network hop, no shared KV — so a
tenant can only ever evaluate its own flags.

get.summary: Returns the caller's flag change log newest-first: every create, update and delete, with the actor and the time.
get.description:
Returns the caller's flag change log newest-first: every
create, update and delete, with the actor and the time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned. 1–500; anything else takes the default 100.

post.summary: Runs the caller's flag definitions for one identity and returns the flag verdict: which flags are on (or which variant), their payloads, and whether any definition failed to compute.
post.description:
Runs the caller's flag definitions for one identity and returns the
flag verdict: which flags are on (or which variant), their payloads,
and whether any definition failed to compute. Evaluation is in-process over the
caller's own (org, project) definitions — no network hop, no shared KV — so a
tenant can only ever evaluate its own flags.

get.summary: Returns every flag definition in the caller's (org, project) store, by key, with its version and who last changed it.
get.description:
Returns every flag definition in the caller's (org,
project) store, by key, with its version and who last changed it.

delete.summary: Removes one flag definition by key and records the deletion in the change log.
delete.description:
Removes one flag definition by key and records the
deletion in the change log. A key the caller's store does not hold is a 404.
A staged capability's key is a SuperAdmin's to remove, as it is to set, and
every other key an owner's or admin's of the org.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the flag key to act on, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one flag definition by key, or 404 when the caller's store has none under that key.
get.description:
Returns one flag definition by key, or 404 when the caller's
store has none under that key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the flag key to act on, from the path.

put.summary: Creates or replaces the flag definition at the path's key and returns the stored row.
put.description:
Creates or replaces the flag definition at the path's key and
returns the stored row. The BODY IS THE DEFINITION DOCUMENT — the flag-definition
JSON object the evaluator consumes — and it is stored verbatim except that its
"key" is forced to the key in the URL, so a document can never be filed under a
name other than the one it was addressed by. Every write bumps the version and
appends to the change log under the caller's identity. A key that lets an org
into a capability that is not ga — research, machines — is a SuperAdmin's to
set, never an org admin's, and its write is on the audit trail before it lands;
every other key is an owner's or admin's of the org, never a member's.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key is the flag key to write, from the path.

get.summary: Reports that the flag engine is serving.
get.description:
Reports that the flag engine is serving. It is not gated: liveness must
be probe-able without a token.

get.summary: Answers the signed-in caller's opt-in to public betas: whether they opted in, whether the org they act in blocked it, and which betas are public.
get.description:
Answers the signed-in caller's opt-in to public betas: whether they
opted in, whether the org they act in blocked it, and which betas are public. A
beta not listed is private, granted person by person.

put.summary: Sets the signed-in caller's OWN opt-in to public betas: on, every public beta and each one promoted later is on for them; off, none is.
put.description:
Sets the signed-in caller's OWN opt-in to public betas: on, every
public beta and each one promoted later is on for them; off, none is. Self only:
the row written is the caller's validated subject, whatever the request says.
Opting in while the org they act in blocked it is refused; opting out never is.

put.summary: Blocks or unblocks the opt-in to public betas for every member of the org the caller acts in.
put.description:
Blocks or unblocks the opt-in to public betas for every member of
the org the caller acts in. An owner or admin of that org, or a SuperAdmin, may;
a member may not. It only withholds: blocked, no member gets a public beta by
opting in, and their own choices are kept for when it is lifted; it never turns
a beta on. A shared sign-up org has no admin to speak for its members and is
refused. The change is on the audit trail before it lands.

get.summary: Answers the platform switches that are decided per caller — `beta`, whether the caller sees what is not yet generally available — as they apply to the signed-in caller: its validated org and user, never anything the request states.
get.description:
Answers the platform switches that are decided per caller — `beta`,
whether the caller sees what is not yet generally available — as they apply to
the signed-in caller: its validated org and user, never anything the request
states. A SuperAdmin targets them from the admin cockpit; nothing here changes
them. A request without a signed-in principal is refused, and a switch that
cannot be read is 503, which a caller takes as off.

action.description: Action is one of created, updated, deleted.

actor.description:
Actor is the email of the principal who made the change. Empty for a write
by an in-process composer; a project key can never appear here, because
evaluating flags is all a key may do.

at.description: At is when the change was made, RFC 3339 UTC.

detail.description:
Detail is free-form context about the change. Nothing writes it today, so
it is absent from every row the store serves.

id.description:
ID is the log's own sequence number, rising with each entry. The log is
served newest-first, which is this descending.

key.description:
Key is the flag that changed. It survives a delete, so the log still names
flags the definition store no longer holds.

definition.description:
Definition is the flag-definition document the evaluator consumes, kept
BYTE-FOR-BYTE as it was written. It is the engine's format rather than this
package's, so it carries fields no Go type here names — targeting groups,
rollout percentages, variants, payloads — and a caller must round-trip it
whole rather than rebuilding it from the parts it recognizes.

key.description:
Key is the flag's primary key in the caller's (org, project) store, and the
name evaluation looks it up by. On a write it is taken from the URL, never
from the body: the stored document's own "key" is forced to match.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is when the definition was last written, RFC 3339 UTC.

updated_by.description:
UpdatedBy is the email of the principal who last wrote it. Empty when the
write came from an in-process composer (an experiment registering its own
assignment flag) rather than from a signed-in person.

version.description:
Version is 1 when the key was created and rises by one on every overwrite.
It counts writes, not content changes: re-storing an identical document
bumps it.

data.description: Data is the change log newest-first: who created, updated or deleted which key, when.
Data is every definition in the caller's (org, project) store, by key.

deleted.description: Deleted is the key that no longer exists.

distinct_id.description: DistinctID is the identity the flags are evaluated for. Required.

groups.description: Groups are the group-level properties, keyed by group type index.

person_properties.description: PersonProperties are the person-level properties conditions match against.

engine.description: Engine names the evaluator this deployment runs.

ok.description: OK is true whenever the flag engine is serving.

on.description:
On opts the caller in to every public beta, current and future, when true,
and out when false.

blocked.description:
Blocked is true when the org the caller acts in turned the opt-in off for
its members. Their own choice is kept and applies again once unblocked.

on.description:
On is true when the caller opted in: every public beta, and each one
promoted later, is on for them unless Blocked.

public.description:
Public is the id of every beta anyone may opt in to (beta.<id>). The rest are
private: a SuperAdmin grants them, person by person.

blocked.description:
Blocked turns the opt-in off for every member of the org when true, and back
on when false. It never turns a beta on for anyone.
Blocked is true when the org's members do not get public betas by opting in.

flags.description:
Flags maps each principal switch's key to whether it is on for the caller:
`beta` is whether the caller sees products and catalog items that are not
yet generally available, and beta.<id> whether they see that one app in
beta in the Hanzo app.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
